Preparing images for a website involves: Preparing images for a website involves more than reducing file size: dimensions, transparency and visual quality also need attention. Repeating those checks one file at a time is slow.
Tiny Image combines browser-side compres: Tiny Image combines browser-side compression with a batch queue, adjustable output settings, visual comparison and downloads. A Worker runs the processing pipeline and loads the required codecs on demand.
This overview is based on the project so: This overview is based on the project source. The configured website, image.tinystool.org, could not be reached over HTTPS during the October 17, 2026 check. Its visit button is temporarily hidden; live deployment has not been verified.
JPEG, PNG and static WebP inputs are pro: JPEG, PNG and static WebP inputs are processed in the browser using Worker and WASM codecs.
Keeping an original PNG without resizing: Keeping an original PNG without resizing uses OxiPNG. If optimization does not reduce its size, the original bytes are retained.
Keep the input format, or convert to JPE: Keep the input format, or convert to JPEG or PNG. Explicit PNG conversion can use color quantization; converting a transparent image to JPEG uses a white background.
Keep the original dimensions or set a ma: Keep the original dimensions or set a maximum long edge, including 1920, 1280, 800 pixels and custom values. Smaller images are not enlarged.
Add files by selection, drag-and-drop or: Add files by selection, drag-and-drop or paste. Cancel tasks, retry failures, or recompress the batch after changing settings.
Inspect a sliding before-and-after compa: Inspect a sliding before-and-after comparison, review file sizes, and download individual images or a ZIP archive.
Supports static JPEG, PNG and WebP input: Supports static JPEG, PNG and WebP inputs. AVIF, HEIC, SVG and animated images are not supported in this version.
The current defaults allow 20 files per: The current defaults allow 20 files per batch and 30 MiB per file, with pixel limits of 32 MP on desktop and 16 MP on mobile. ZIP downloads have a 100 MiB safety limit.
Savings depend on the source and setting: Savings depend on the source and settings. Lossy encoding, quantization and resizing can change image appearance; compare the result before using it.
Set dimensions for the intended display: Set dimensions for the intended display size, compress the batch and inspect important details before downloading.
For a PNG that must retain its pixels, k: For a PNG that must retain its pixels, keep the original format and dimensions. Review shadows and translucent edges in the comparison view.
Deliver a batch of content images: Deliver a batch of content images
Use one set of output options across the: Use one set of output options across the queue, retry individual failures and package the finished images into a ZIP.
Are images sent to a compression server?: Are images sent to a compression server?
The inspected processing pipeline runs l: The inspected processing pipeline runs locally in the browser, using Worker and WASM codecs rather than a server compression API. This is a source-level finding, not a new production network audit.
No. Original PNG optimization without re: No. Original PNG optimization without resizing has a lossless path. JPEG encoding, PNG quantization and resizing must not be described as preserving every original pixel.
